messages.subject: Improving Efficiency of GLMM
parts:
Hi all,

I'm having trouble recreating this GLM model for mass-spectrometry data which was originally written using the MCMCglmm package for R (see MCMCglmmExample.R with input data protein.Rdata and ee.Rdata, both attached).

Which I've ported to Stan (model.stan, input data is model_1.data.R, both attached; model.stan shown below):
data {
  int<lower=1> num_datapoints;
  int<lower=1> num_spectra;
  int<lower=1> num_runchannels;
  int<lower=1> num_conditions;

  int<lower=1> num_peptides;
  int<lower=1> num_digests;

  int<lower=1> num_samplepopulations; //num unique sample-population combinations
  int<lower=1> num_populations;

  int<lower=1,upper=num_populations> populationID[num_samplepopulations];
  int<lower=0,upper=1> singleSample[num_populations]; //indicator for populations with only one sample

  int<lower=0,upper=num_populations> num_singleSamples; //total num populations with only one sample
  int<lower=0,upper=num_singleSamples> cumsumsingleSample[num_populations];

  int<lower=0> count[num_datapoints];

  vector[num_runchannels-1] eemean;
  vector<lower=0>[num_runchannels-1] eesd;

  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_spectra] U; //design matrix for runchannel effect
  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_runchannels-1] V; //design matrix for spectrum effect
  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_conditions-1] W; //etc.
  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_digests*num_peptides] X;
  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_samplepopulations] Y;
  matrix <lower=0,upper=1> [num_datapoints,num_spectra] Z; //design matrix for residual variances

}

parameters {
  vector[num_spectra] beta_spectrum;
  vector[num_runchannels-1] beta_runchannel;
  vector[num_conditions-1] beta_condition;

  vector[num_digests*num_peptides] epsilon_digest_raw;
  vector[num_samplepopulations] epsilon_sample_raw;

  vector<lower=0>[num_populations-num_singleSamples] sigma_population_fake;
  vector<lower=0>[num_peptides] sigma_peptide;

  vector<lower=0>[num_spectra] sigma_spectrum;

  vector[num_datapoints]lambda_raw;
}

transformed parameters{
  vector[num_datapoints] lambda;

  vector<lower=0>[num_populations] sigma_population;
  vector[num_samplepopulations] epsilon_sample;
  vector[num_digests*num_peptides] epsilon_digest;

  for (P in 1:num_populations){
    if(singleSample[P] == 1){ //populations with only one sample given sd=~0
      sigma_population[P] <- 1E-10;
    }else{
      sigma_population[P] <- sigma_population_fake[P-cumsumsingleSample[P]];
    }
  }

  for (S in 1:num_samplepopulations)
    epsilon_sample[S] <- sigma_population[populationID[S]] * epsilon_sample_raw[S];

  for (D in 1:num_digests)
    for (P in 1:num_peptides)
      epsilon_digest[(D-1)*num_peptides + P] <- sigma_peptide[P] * epsilon_digest_raw[(D-1)*num_peptides + P];

  lambda <- U*beta_spectrum -1 + V*beta_runchannel + W*beta_condition + X*epsilon_digest + Y*epsilon_sample + Z*sigma_spectrum .* lambda_raw;

}
model {
  beta_spectrum ~ normal(0.0,10);
  beta_runchannel ~ normal(eemean,eesd);
  beta_condition ~ normal(0.0,10);

  epsilon_sample_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  epsilon_digest_raw ~ normal(0,1);

  sigma_peptide ~ cauchy(0,5);
  sigma_population_fake ~ cauchy(0,5);

  sigma_spectrum  ~ cauchy(0,5);

  lambda_raw ~ normal(0,1);

  count ~ poisson(exp(lambda));
}

We have fixed effects for Spectrum, RunChannel and Condition. The RunChannel fixed effect is given a strong prior since it's just the offset compared to channel 0 due to volume differences. Sample and Digest are random effects with standard deviations per Population and Peptide respectively. A population's sd is set to ~0 if the population is represented by only one sample in the data.  Finally, residual variances are per Spectrum.

The model runs and the output is correct, but it's incredibly slow in comparison (~700 seconds compared to ~1 second for 10,000 iterations), which I could forgive if the effective sample sizes for many of the parameters (e.g. beta_spectrum and beta_condition) weren't so much smaller than those obtained in MCMCglmm. I'm using Stan.jl, so have been importing the samples from MCMCglmm into a Mamba.Chains object in Julia and checking ESS for both MCMCglmm and Stan with Mamba.jl's summarystats() for consistency (see MCMCglmmSummaryStats.txt and StanSummaryStats.txt attached).

For example, the spectrum effects:

Stan:

beta_spectrum.1     98.242555
beta_spectrum.2     72.485770
beta_spectrum.3     81.562845
beta_spectrum.4    114.097882
beta_spectrum.5     75.931559
beta_spectrum.6    156.050094

MCMCglmm:
                ESS   
Spectrum1    2392.21453
Spectrum2    2396.86139
Spectrum3    2141.83108
Spectrum4    3189.64711
Spectrum5    2001.76688
Spectrum6    3954.65690

Any help that anyone can offer in getting this running comparably, both in terms of sample size and samples per second, would be greatly appreciated. Apologies for the lengthy post.

Cheers,
Al
